record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Grammatical Inference
record.original_question: What is the learnability theory for deterministic partially observable Markov decision processes? The source model has states Q, input alphabet Σ, initial state q0, a probabilistic transition function, and a probabilistic reward function; in the deterministic case, each state-action pair has a unique next state with probability 1. The open problem asks how such deterministic POMDPs can be learned, including whether identification in the limit with probability 1 or reinforcement-learning-style convergence criteria are appropriate.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) is given by a finite set of states Q, a finite input alphabet Σ, an initial state q0 ∈ Q, a probabilistic transition function δ : Q × Σ × Q → [0,1] with Σ_{q'} δ(q,a,q') = 1 for every q ∈ Q and a ∈ Σ, and a probabilistic reward function. The POMDP is called deterministic when for every state q ∈ Q and every action a ∈ Σ there exists a (necessarily unique) state q' ∈ Q with δ(q,a,q') = 1. Develop a learnability theory for the class of deterministic POMDPs: specify a suitable learning criterion (for example, identification in the limit with probability 1, or convergence in a reinforcement-learning sense) and design an algorithm that, given access to interactions or sample trajectories with rewards, provably learns an unknown deterministic POMDP under the chosen criterion; in particular, determine whether such POMDPs are identifiable in the limit with probability 1 from a polynomial amount of data and characterize the appropriate efficiency and convergence guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: A search yields work on deterministic POMDPs (e.g., planning-side revisits) and on learning stochastic deterministic automata, but no published result establishes a full learnability theory for deterministic POMDPs in a grammatical-inference sense (identification in the limit with probability 1 or reinforcement-learning convergence guarantees). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ten Open Problems in Grammatical Inference
status_evidence.claim: Learning deterministic POMDPs is listed among open problems in grammatical inference.

status_evidence.title: Deterministic POMDPs Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Deterministic POMDPs with deterministic actions and observations are challenging because observations only partially identify states.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses planning in deterministic POMDPs but not a full learnability theory.

status_evidence.title: Learning Stochastic Deterministic Regular Languages
status_evidence.snippet: Stochastic deterministic finite automata cannot be identified from only a polynomial quantity of data under identification in the limit with probability one.
status_evidence.claim: Related identification-in-the-limit results suggest negative polynomial-data results, indicating the POMDP learnability question is nontrivial and not resolved.
